extracted.intended_audience: students and readers learning arithmetic and root-extraction algorithms (historical/early-modern audience)
extracted.subtask_description: A chapter-like exposition giving procedural rules for extracting square, cube, and higher roots, for multiplying/duplicating/tripling numbers, for adding/subtracting radicands, and for giving geometric demonstrations of these arithmetic procedures. It is an instructional/textbook treatment aimed at teaching how to operate on numbers and their geometric analogues.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principles for root extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and methods to extract roots (square, cube, and higher): group the number into periods appropriate to the root (pairs for square, triples for cube), find successive digits of the root by selecting the greatest possible term whose power fits the current partial dividend, subtract, bring down the next period, and continue iteratively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains grouping digits into periods, repeatedly choosing the largest trial digit, subtracting the corresponding power or product, and bringing down the next group. Notes there are many possible ways to perform the same operation and discusses reducing some cases to simpler known forms (e.g., reducing to square extraction). Mentions the need for memory of squares/cubes and tables to speed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for extracting square roots
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific method for square root extraction: partition the number into pairs (periods) from the units place, find the greatest square ≤ the first period, subtract it, bring down the next pair, double the current root to form a trial divisor, choose the next digit to multiply the trial divisor (with that digit) giving the largest product ≤ the current remainder, subtract and repeat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicitly uses the long-division style root algorithm: form periods of two digits, use doubled root as the divisor for next step, select the digit that fits, and iterate. Recommends treating pure square numbers and supplementing with geometric figure demonstrations for clarity. Advises reducing some problems to this canonical procedure when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for extracting cube roots
rubrics_metrics.description: Cube-root extraction by grouping digits into triples and using successive approximations: use the cube of the trial leading digit and subtract, then use combinations involving doubled/tripled previous partial root to form the appropriate trial multiplicative terms for the next digit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentions grouping into triple periods and that analogous but more complicated combinations (involving squares and products of previous partial root with new trial digit) are used than in the square root case. Recommends knowing cubes and related products to pick correct trial digits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to lower-order cases (reducing higher roots to squares/cubes)
rubrics_metrics.description: When possible, reduce complicated root-extraction or product computations to previously handled lower-degree cases (e.g., reduce certain forms to square extraction or to multiplication rules already established).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that many operations can be handled by transforming the expression into forms whose solution is given by earlier rules; gives examples (reducing to square/cube, or reducing radicals by duplicating factors). Encourages memorizing standard reductions to simplify repeated work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplication, triplication and multiple-of-a-number rules (doubling, tripling, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for obtaining multiples of numbers (duplare, triplar, quadruplicare): how to double/triple numbers, how these operations interact with root/extraction procedures and with geometric figures (e.g., doubling a side affects square/cube areas/volumes in a predictable way).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains duplication as used in extracting roots and in constructing trial divisors (e.g., doubling the current root). Shows how to interpret duplication geometrically (doubling side produces quadrupling area etc.), and how multiples are used when combining terms during root extraction and multiplication-by-constant steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplication methods and multiple modes of performing products
rubrics_metrics.description: Many modes of multiplying numbers are possible; the text enumerates several operational ways to multiply and to use multiplication to aid other operations (e.g., in root extraction or reducing remainders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes that there are multiple equivalent methods to multiply and to use products in algorithms; recommends choosing the most convenient (often the one that reduces the problem to known rules). Illustrates how multiplication by parts, by grouping, or by using binomial decomposition can simplify work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of pure powers versus mixed/composite quantities
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguishes 'pure' numbers (pure powers like perfect squares or cubes) from composite quantities; rules differ when radicands or factors are pure powers versus mixtures. Pure numbers simplify root extraction and duplication operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes identifying when numbers are pure powers (so duplication/triplication yields simpler patterns) and when they are mixtures that must be manipulated via the general algorithms. Advises recognizing pure-power structure to shortcut calculations and to know when geometric arguments apply directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for adding and subtracting radicands (operations between roots)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on when roots/radicands may be added or subtracted directly and when they must first be reduced to a common form or decomposed into pure parts; includes procedures for subtracting roots and managing remainders during such operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that some combinations cannot be simplified and that one must follow specific steps (similar to long arithmetic) to combine roots: align corresponding periods, perform subtraction with borrow where needed, and apply the root-extraction algorithm to the remainder. Warns about illegitimate simplifications (implicit anti-pattern: adding unlike radical types as if like terms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of remainders and iterative choice of trial digits
rubrics_metrics.description: When a trial digit produces a product less than the current partial dividend, subtract it and bring down the next period; continue by choosing the next trial digit according to doubled/tripled prior partial roots combined with the new digit's contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives stepwise iterative guidance: choose greatest fitting trial digit, subtract its composed product, then bring down next grouped period and repeat. Notes the sequence of operations and the algebraic terms (products of previous partial root with the new digit, and powers of the new digit) that determine the subtraction amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping of digits into periods appropriate to the root
rubrics_metrics.description: For root extraction, digits must be partitioned into periods of length equal to the index of the root (pairs for square roots, triples for cube roots, etc.), starting from the units place to the left (and from decimal point to right if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that correct grouping is essential to the algorithm; shows examples (pairs for squares, triples for cubes), and indicates how bringing down the next period supplies the next partial dividend for the iterative step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric demonstrations of arithmetic rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Use geometric figures (squares, cubes, rectangles, right triangles) to demonstrate and justify the arithmetic rules for roots and multiplicative relations: e.g., interpreting square root extraction as finding a side whose square equals the given area, and duplications/triplications via constructed figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommends showing the rule by building geometric figures that represent the algebraic quantities (construct a square, add and arrange supplementary rectangles or squares to illustrate the algebraic decomposition used in the algorithm). The text argues that geometric demonstrations make the rules clearer to the reader/auditor and serve as validation of the algebraic procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of tabulated powers and memorization to speed calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Memorize squares, cubes, and common products to make trial-digit selection and multiplication steps quicker during root extraction and other arithmetic work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises that knowledge of small powers and standard products (tables) allows one to pick trial digits without lengthy multiplication; indicates that practice and memory (e.g., knowing 2^2,3^2,... and cubes) materially ease the iterative process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality and applicability of the rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of rules given are presented as universal procedures applicable to all numbers of the relevant type; when followed they will produce the correct root or product regardless of the particular numbers involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that the rules are not ad hoc but general; the chapter repeatedly emphasizes that although there are many ways to proceed in particular cases, the canonical rules work universally. Encourages applying the provided general methods rather than inventing incompatible shortcuts without reference to the reduction steps given.
